problem: Zero-shot object navigation systems, both map-centric and VLM-based, pick actions with a single-pass Top-1 score. This compresses goal progress, uncertainty and reliability into one scalar, so errors are overconfident and there is no early self-correction, which causes long detours and redundant exploration.
motivation: Reliable navigation under partial observability needs evidence cross-checking before an action is executed. Homogeneous multi-agent debate tends to reinforce shared mistakes, so the paper uses heterogeneous, complementary stances over a shared candidate action set.
key_idea: Replace one-shot candidate scoring with a training-free debate between a goal-progress stance (TSU) and a safety/information-auditing stance (SIB), then arbitrate with an NCA judge that optionally triggers a soft-compromise micro-probing step.
insight: The gains come from the decision structure rather than the backbone, since it works with the lightweight Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite. Ablations on HM3Dv2 show both stances are needed (TSU-only SR 62.4, SIB-only 56.5 vs full 73.0), and removing NCA drops SR to 67.8. Debate rounds saturate at 3 (SR 51.3 -> 65.6 -> 73.0 -> 73.5 for 1/2/3/4 rounds), and micro-probing adds a small SPL/AORI gain (SPL 36.9 -> 38.7).
method: Candidate/context interface: a WMNav-style geometry-aware generator proposes polar candidates (r, θ); Φ wraps them into candidate cards with step-local ids and direction descriptions, together with goal text and optional evidence.
TSU agent: proposes the candidate most likely to advance the goal from target semantics, observation, scene layout, history and evidence, and returns an id, rationale and evidence each round.
SIB agent: a goal-deemphasized auditor of risk, traversability, visibility and premature commitment. It returns agree, or counter with a grounded deficiency and an executable alternative candidate.
Multi-round debate: up to K=3 rounds (default), stopping early on agreement, producing a structured trace D_t of preferences, rationales and evidence, with support/rebuttal relations.

NCA arbitration agent: reads the candidates and full trace and picks the final action under unified task/safety/information criteria; if disagreement persists it selects one of the two final preferences.

Two-mode execution: Mode A executes the NCA action directly. Mode B applies when the stances disagree and |Δθ|≤α, using micro-probing with r=β_r·r*, θ=θ*+β_θ·Δθ, (β_r,β_θ)=(1/2,1/3), to acquire disambiguating views.

setting.backbone: Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite (frozen, prompted VLM; also Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and GPT-4.1-nano in the ablation)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (first-person), with target text goal
setting.action_space: continuous polar candidates: stop, rotate, move_forward with distance in [0.5 m, 1.7 m]
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, MP3D) plus a real robot

numbers.eval_set_note: paper says HM3Dv1 GOAT val unseen

numbers_note: HM3D-ObjNav is listed with split 'val' as printed, since the paper only says 'validation splits'. HM3Dv1 and HM3Dv2 are separate entries with the same benchmark label. Debate-metric table (DR/JOR/MPTR) omitted.
results: DSCD-Nav reaches 75.6/40.1 SR/SPL on HM3Dv1, 73.0/38.7 on HM3Dv2 and 47.8/24.2 on MP3D with a lightweight Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite, beating the strongest baselines in the table (CogNav 72.5 SR on HM3Dv1, VLFM 63.6 SR on HM3Dv2, OneMap 37.4 SPL). Among training-free VLM baselines on HM3Dv2 it beats DORAEMON (62.0/23.0) and cuts AORI to 39.2; on GOAT it reaches 40.1/32.3 vs 24.3/10.3.
limitations: Multi-round VLM calls per step (three agents and up to K rounds) raise inference cost and latency; real-world inference runs on a remote A6000 server.
Depends on an upstream candidate generator (WMNav-style) and on VLM quality: SR drops to 58.7 with GPT-4.1-nano.
Real-world evaluation is only qualitative (sofa and plant targets), with no quantitative results.
